title: Finite closed-cover resolution with its actual adjunction augmentation
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $A$ a sheaf of commutative rings on its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] with rings obtained by inverse image [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], and ordinary derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] and let $Z_1,\ldots,Z_m\hookrightarrow X$, $m\geq1$, be closed immersions factoring through $Z$ whose underlying closed subsets cover $Z$. Assume the complementary open immersions $X\setminus Z\hookrightarrow X$ and $X\setminus Z_a\hookrightarrow X$ are quasi-compact morphisms (not merely that their sources are quasi-compact spaces). For $\varnothing\ne J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}$ let $Z_J=\bigcap_{a\in J}Z_a$ be the scheme-theoretic intersection and $i_J:Z_J\hookrightarrow X$ its inclusion. Use the actual closed adjunction units and exact closed direct images [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed].
For every bounded-below complex $K$ of $A$-module sheaves, the alternating closed-restriction complex has a natural augmented quasi-isomorphism
$$i_*i^*K\longrightarrow\left[\bigoplus_{|J|=1}i_{J,*}i_J^*K\longrightarrow\bigoplus_{|J|=2}i_{J,*}i_J^*K\longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow i_{\{1,\ldots,m\},*}i_{\{1,\ldots,m\}}^*K\right].$$
The bracket denotes the finite total complex with the singleton term in horizontal degree zero; its differential is the signed sum of the actual restriction units for $J\subset J\cup\{a\}$. Its augmentation composed with $K\to i_*i^*K$ is exactly the direct sum of the units $K\to i_{a,*}i_a^*K$. This is an identification in the derived category, natural in $K$, refinements of a finite ordered closed covering, and pullbacks for which the closed-restriction comparison maps are identified. In particular it is compatible with automorphisms of such diagrams, including parameterized diagrams. No assertion that the $Z_a\to Z$ form a covering of the pro-etale site is made.

proof.text: Use the signed-restriction lemma to form $D^{-1}=E_Z$ and $D^p=\bigoplus_{|J|=p+1}E_J$, with its actual restriction-unit differential. It gives $d^2=0$ and $\alpha_M\eta_i=(\eta_{i_a})_a$, naturally in $M$.

proof.text: On each affine open $V\subset X$, the vertex-contraction lemma makes every $i_{a,V}^*D(M|_V)$ contractible and the restriction of $D(M|_V)$ to $U_V=V\setminus|Z\times_XV|$ zero. For a cohomology sheaf $H$ of $D(M|_V)$, exact inverse images preserve homology, so $j_{U_V}^*H=0$ and every $i_{a,V}^*H=0$; with inverse-image coefficient rings the module inverse image has the abelian inverse image as underlying sheaf. The morphisms $U_V\hookrightarrow V$ (base change of the quasi-compact $X\setminus Z\hookrightarrow X$) and $Z_a\times_XV\hookrightarrow V$ (closed immersions) are finitely many quasi-compact maps whose images cover $|V|$, as the $|Z_a|$ cover $|Z|$. Finite quasi-compact detection applied to $\mathrm{id}_H$ gives $H=0$. The open-restriction and locality assertions of the contraction lemma give exactness on $X$: $E_Z(M)[0]\to D^{\geq0}(M)$ is a quasi-isomorphism for every $M$.

proof.text: Apply the natural additive row construction to each $K^q$. Its differentials commute with $d_K$. Totalize with $d_D+(-1)^p d_K$ and column bound $r=m$. The nonnegative row complex is zero for $p<0$ or $m\leq p$; every total diagonal is finite. Put $A^\bullet=E_Z(K)$ and $a_q=\alpha_{K^q}$. The specified augmentation has component $a_q$ followed by the $(0,q)$ inclusion, and the preceding row quasi-isomorphisms have precisely these zero components. The finite-strip row-augmentation lemma therefore proves this total augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism. Exactness of $E_Z$ gives $H^n(E_ZK)=E_ZH^n(K)$, so it preserves quasi-isomorphisms. The natural augmentation square and two-out-of-three imply that $C$ also does. Localization yields the natural derived isomorphism for bounded-below $K$.

source.place: Tag 0133, lemma-double-complex-gives-resolution, second-variable variant; applied through lem-sc-finite-strip-row-augmentation to the finite horizontal strip and its specified column-zero augmentation.

proof.text: For a refinement the signed-restriction lemma gives the sorting-sign chain map $\rho_f$ (zero on repeated image indices) and $\rho_f\alpha_Z=\alpha_W$, also after totalization. The finer family $W$ again covers $Z$ with quasi-compact complements, so steps 2 and 3 apply to it; since both augmentations are invertible in the derived category, $Q\rho_f=Q\alpha_W(Q\alpha_Z)^{-1}$. This proves independence of the refinement function and compatibility with iterated refinements.

proof.text: For a pullback with the stipulated unit-compatible closed comparisons, the total-pullback lemma identifies every face and pins the total map on all diagonal inclusions. The members $Z_a\times_XX'$ cover $Z\times_XX'$ with quasi-compact complements (base change), so steps 1–3 make $\alpha'$ a quasi-isomorphism. The square $\tau\,g^*\alpha=\alpha'c_Z$, with $\tau$ and $c_Z$ chain isomorphisms, makes $g^*\alpha$ one by two-out-of-three. The lemma gives the derived normalization. Its natural-transformation identities give compatibility with automorphisms and parameter diagrams, with the refinement and $K$-naturality above.

lean.statement:
theorem finite_closed_cover_resolution {X Z : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X)
    [IsClosedImmersion i] (m : ℕ) (hm : 0 < m) (W : Fin m → Over X)
    (hclosed : ∀ a, IsClosedImmersion (W a).hom)
    (hfactor : ∀ a, Nonempty (W a ⟶ Over.mk i))
    (hcover : Set.range i = ⋃ a, Set.range (W a).hom)
    (hqc : ∃ U : X.Opens, Set.range U.ι = (Set.range i)ᶜ ∧ QuasiCompact U.ι)
    (hqcW : ∀ a, ∃ U : X.Opens,
      Set.range U.ι = (Set.range (W a).hom)ᶜ ∧ QuasiCompact U.ι)
    (A : Sheaf (ProEt.topology X) CommRingCat.{u + 1}) : ∃ D : FiniteClosedResolution i W A,
      FiniteClosedRefinementCompatible D ∧ FiniteClosedPullbackCompatible D
